title: The Delay Line
subtitle: From a repair shop in Kingston to the empty spaces in English rock

intro.age7: Follow an echo from Jamaica all the way to London.
intro.age13: A man who fixed radios in Kingston figured out that you could take a song apart and make the leftover space into the music. Follow that idea across an ocean and watch it change punk.
intro.adult: Traces the dub structural logic from Tubby and Perry into English punk and post-punk, and shows the difference between surface borrowing and structural transfer.

framing.age13: Start in Kingston with King Tubby, who repaired electronics for a living and rebuilt his own mixing desk. His idea was to take a finished song apart and let the gaps become the music.
framing.adult: The thread starts with a technique rather than a record: a mixing desk used to take things away, so that space and echo carry the track.

framing.age13: Lee Perry was working in Kingston in the same years. By 1977 a song he had produced turned up on a London punk album, covered by the Clash and six minutes long.
framing.adult: The first crossing is a cover: a Perry production carried into a punk album more or less as a song, which is borrowing at the surface.

framing.age13: Next the Clash brought Perry himself to London to produce them. Listen to how little the result sounds like his own records: a studio sound is hard to carry across.
framing.adult: The second crossing moves a person rather than a song. The distance between the finished single and Perry's own studio sound is the point of this stop.

framing.age13: The deepest crossing comes last. PiL took dub's shape, not its sound: the bass in front, the guitar as texture, the silence on purpose.
framing.adult: The thread ends on structural transfer, the kind of influence that is hardest to document, which is why this edge is held at consensus rather than documented.

outro.age7: The echo kept travelling and it never really stopped.
outro.age13: The same idea turns up later in Bristol, in jungle, and in almost every record with a lot of space in it.
outro.adult: Terminates at PiL for now. Extend forward through Bristol and dubstep in Track D.
